data.name: Awmani
data.gender_notes: Awmani is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic word 'awmanah', meaning 'gifted' or 'generous'. It is a name with deep spiritual significance in Islam, symbolizing the bestowal of blessings and kindness. The name Awmani carries the meaning “Gifted, Generous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Awmani usually hope their child will grow to embody gifted, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies generosity and kindness.
data.etymology: Awmani belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gifted, Generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Awmani total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: أوماني
in_arabic.meaning: الأمن و الرفاهية و السعادة في الحياة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أوماني مشتق من الجذر العربي (أمن) الذي يحمل معاني الأمن والسلام والاستقرار، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع مثل 'وَأَمنِ مِنهُمُ اللَّهُ' (سورة التوبة: 6)، ويعني الاسم هنا الحالة النفسية والمعيشية المستقرة والآمنة، مما يجعله من الأسماء المحببة في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: اومانی
in_urdu.meaning: زندگی میں امن، خوشحالی اور سکون کا مطلب
in_urdu.long_meaning: اومانی نام عربی جڑ (أمن) سے نکلا ہے، جس کے معنی ہیں محفوظ، سکون اور استحکام، قرآن مجید میں اس جڑ کا ذکر 'وَأَمنِ مِنهُمُ اللَّهُ' (التوبة: 6) جیسی آیات میں ملتا ہے، یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں ایک خوبصورت اور معنی خیز انتخاب کے طور پر دیکھا جاتا ہے

in_hindi.name: औमानी
in_hindi.meaning: जीवन में शांति, समृद्धि और सुरक्षा का तात्पर्य
in_hindi.long_meaning: औमानी नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी मूल (أمن) से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है सुरक्षा, शांति और स्थिरता, इस मूल का उल्लेख कुरआन में 'وَأَمنِ مِنهُمُ اللَّهُ' (तौबा: 6) जैसी आयतों में मिलता है, यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में एक अच्छा और अर्थपूर्ण नाम माना जाता है

in_pashto.name: اومنی
in_pashto.meaning: په ژوند کې د امن، سوکالۍ او ارامش معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: اومنی نوم د عربي ريښې (أمن) څخه اخيستل شوی دی، کوم چې د امن، سولې او ثبات معنی لري، قرآن کريم کې يې د 'وَأَمنِ مِنهُمُ اللَّهُ' (التوبة: 6) په څير آيتونو کې يادونه شوې ده، دا نوم د افغان او پښتن تراد کې يو ښکلی او مانا ور نوم ګڼل کيږي

in_english.name: Awmani
in_english.meaning: Conveys security, prosperity, and peace in life
in_english.long_meaning: The name Awmani originates from the Arabic root (أمن) signifying safety, peace, and stability, mentioned in Quranic verses such as 'وَأَمنِ مِنهُمُ اللَّهُ' (At-Tawbah: 6), it symbolizes a state of psychological and material well-being, making it a cherished name in Islamic tradition for its spiritual significance and positive connotations

data.cultural_impact: The name Awmani holds a significant cultural impact in Islamic societies by representing the values of generosity and kindness. A generous person is highly respected in Islamic culture and their actions serve as an inspiration to others.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Awmani underscores the concept of God as the ultimate giver and bestower of all blessings. It is a reminder of the importance of being grateful for the gifts and blessings bestowed upon us, and the obligation to use them in the service of others and for the greater good. The name also encourages the practice of sadaqah (charity) and other acts of generosity, which are considered crucial aspects of Islamic faith and for fulfilling one's purpose in life.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun documents the name Awmani in his ' Muqaddimah '. He mentions it as a Berber tribe in North Africa, active in the 13th and 14th centuries.

Al-Bakri describes the Awmani as a people inhabiting the regions between Morocco and Tunisia. He places their settlements along the coast, with the cities of Susah and Azir being prominent. This description is from around the 11th century.
historical_references.context: People inhabiting regions between Morocco and Tunisia with settlements along the coast
